On 12 July 1995, in the morning hours, the Chetniks again began shelling using all weapons. The wood where there was a large number of our wounded and dead soldiers and civilians, I don't know the exact number." First of all, sir, is this part of your statement that I read out truthful and accurate such that you would stand by the same and testify again if asked about these events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: No. This is a mistake. Not the 12th of July but the 13th of July. The 12th, that was a Wednesday, we spent the whole day travelling from Buljim to Sekovici, that you were mentioning in connection with Nova Kasaba. That was the shelling. And then of course if I think back to the 12th in the evening. It was on the 13th, on Thursday, that it happened. I can see the 12th here. Maybe it was their mistake when they were writing it down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir. Apart from the correction of the date, is the remainder of what I have read from this section truthful and accurate such that you would so testify again today, subject to the solemn declaration, if asked about these same events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Yes, I'd say so. There was a large number of wounded and dead lying in that brook.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, if we could return to your Rule 92 ter statement, P1547, at page 3 in the English, it's the second paragraph from the bottom, and in B/C/S, it's page 3 but the third paragraph from the bottom. And while we wait for that, sir, I can perhaps tell you what I believe it says and what my request for clarification is. In that portion of your 92 ter statement you talk about the fact that you tried many roads but were ambushed and that you heard that many people were killed in the river area but did not see this. Now, first, I would like to be clear that the persons that are described in this paragraph of your 92 ter statement that would have been killed in the river area we are still talking about casualties from the fighting and shooting coming from the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: I didn't understand you properly. Can you explain and put a brief question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir. If you could look at paragraph number 10 of the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the microphone is --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At paragraph 10 of your statement, sir, in both languages as it's marked, you say that, "I heard many people were killed in the river area but I did not see this." And my question for you is to clarify that the persons that you would have heard of being killed in the river area as in your statement relates to casualties from the fighting, the shooting, that was being directed at the column of men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: There was no fighting when it comes to our own army. They did not engage in combat. All the people that I saw lying in that stream were killed by shells or snipers and the Praga that was firing from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, now I'm confused. Earlier you testified that you were not close enough to the front of the column so as to see or hear whether they were shooting, now you're saying that no one from your army engaged in any fighting. How can you account for those inconsistencies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about my group, the group of people I was in. And that place. I could see people from the columns -- from the column who lay dead there in that stream, or who had been seriously wounded. So the fire was on the Serb part throughout that time. As for the forward end of the column, I never mentioned that, nor do I know what was happening there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification. Am I also correct in addition to the river area, there were a lot of bodies of persons killed from the shelling that were along the roadways and that those bodies were just left there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Yes. At first, we began pulling out, and I'm talking about the 12th, to the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear what hill.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We pulled out some 30 wounded or so to a plateau, and there was a major ambush there. Now, what happened to those wounded men, afterwards, I never learned, but the others were left behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now I'd like to move back to your statement that we have on the screen and I believe it's paragraph 12 of the same which is the next page in English and it's the last two lines in B/C/S on the page that we have now. If we could scroll down to that. And here, sir, you are talking about people panicking because there was no way out, and that people started committing suicide. And you say that you saw at least 20 persons with your own eyes who committed suicide and every 4 to 5 metres there was another body. Now I would like to clarify with you, sir, at this point would you agree with me that the people in the column had been broken up into smaller groups, each group going their own direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Yes. I agree the groups had been broken up, but there were attempts to get out on the roads, so my group remained cut off in that section. We were cut off from the main column.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in relation to these 20 persons that you with your own eyes saw commit suicide, would it be accurate to state that these 20 persons were all from or comprising a part of your group that had broken off from the column which was 100 persons in total?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: No. I could not say that. I can't say that these people were from my group. The truth is they were in the column but I can also not confirm that there were 100 men in that column. There were 100 people down below where we surrendered but as from what I could see there were some 20 people or so, I didn't really count them, who lay dead. But how they died, I can't really guarantee, vouchsafe for, but I did see one or two men commit suicide but that these 20 men committed suicide, I can't really confirm that. I did see 20 men lying dead in that stream.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In terms of those that you actually saw yourselves, am I correct that you saw persons shoot their own relatives or that relatives shot each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Yes. I did say that. I did see one such case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: At this time, was there also a dispute and in-fighting amongst the persons that were part of the column between those that wanted to surrender and those that wanted to fight onward and continue to try to break through the Serb lines?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Well, there may have been some differences amongst them, but believe me I couldn't really hear very much. There was a relative of mine who was seriously wounded and I was trying to save him. So the only option left for us was to surrender and when we heard the Serbs calling out on a bull horn to surrender we decided to do it, and we saw an end -- a portion of the column that were moving -- we saw people moving forward and they had a blue UN flag. We also -- so we believed that we would actually manage to get to the -- and be taken to the UNPROFOR soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you find a suitable moment within the next two or three minutes for a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: For those that decided to surrender, were there persons who had been previously wearing military uniforms, who discarded their military uniforms and changed into civilian clothing prior to surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: No. I didn't see any such persons there. I didn't see anyone changing uniform there. It's possible that there were such cases among those who had surrendered earlier, but where I was, I didn't see -- I couldn't see anyone like that. We were all in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where you were, did anyone discard weapons before surrendering?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: No. I didn't see that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are at a suitable point for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we first move into closed session so that the witness can leave the courtroom. And we will resume after the break in closed session again.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to move on to focus on the events that transpired as you -- and I believe you testified 250 to 300 persons proceeded to the asphalt road and surrendered to the soldiers who you say identified themselves as Serb civilian police. Could you confirm for us that at this time no one was executed or mistreated by these persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: No. We corrected that mistake. It was between 100 and 150 people. I don't know how we came to say 250 because that's a large group. What I wanted to say was that when we surrendered to these Serb soldiers, mistreatment and beatings started right away. Many were beaten up already at the spot. We were immediately ordered to surrender all the items we had. We were searched. And this group of soldiers who were there on the road by Sandici took away everything that we had. If we had any gold, jewellery, rings, we had to hand everything over to them. There were several wounded persons by the road side, and there was my relative. We stayed close to them. So the mistreatment and blows started right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that these persons also took away weapons that members of that group of 100 to 150 persons that you were with had on their person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: I didn't even see anybody carry any weapons to the spot where the Serbian soldiers were. Mostly those who surrendered there were unarmed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to call up 1D1031 again, and again as with all the others we should not broadcast. And if we can turn to page 3 in the English, and page 2 in the B/C/S, I think it might be 3 in the B/C/S since they are double-sided. That's fine. That's the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, here in relation -- waiting for the English -- in relation to the surrender, here is what you said on 19 July 1995: "After a while the Chetniks began to call on us through megaphones to surrender, alleging that they would not hurt us and would transport us with our families to Kladanj and Tuzla. Then a large number of us set off walking in file towards them in the village of Mandici where we surrendered. Then they searched us, took away all the weapons we had, money, documents and everything else." Does that refresh your recollection, sir, as to whether members of that group that you surrendered with were armed and those arms were taken away by the Serb forces searching you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Well, yes. What is probably meant here is - and I'm speaking for myself - I had a pistol with me which was a licensed pistol. I had it and got it perhaps 15 years before the war, and it was that pistol that I had on me and I handed it over to the Serb soldier. So perhaps it was along those lines that I gave this statement. There may have been others who did the same but that I saw someone hand over a rifle, no, I didn't. What was in question here was this pistol. So what I was saying here was that I, myself, handed over my pistol to them. And I repeat, it was a licensed pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With relation to the transfer of yourself and others to the football pitch at Kasaba, first of all, am I correct that prior to going to the football pitch at Kasaba you were kept in some rooms at a school in Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Yes. We were held in some rooms, not of a school building, it was a building which was being built before the war and was to become a marketplace, but what you have today is just the walls and concrete slab. So this was the group of us who came from Sandici and there were two other rooms full of people there. So it wasn't a school building. It was just a structure that was in the process of being built at the time, and it still stands like that today.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that while you were at this structure you were provided water, kept for about an hour before being transported to the football pitch at Kasaba? I note that my microphone apparently was out. I would like to repeat the question, then. Sir, is it correct that you were kept at that structure, that location, for about an hour, you were provided water and then you were transferred to the football pitch at Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: I don't know exactly if it was just one hour. At any rate, we were held in that room. There was sweltering heat. The temperature was about 40 degrees, it was between mid-day and 1.00 p.m. Somebody brought over some water from a nearby river, I believe, in pails, you know the sort of pails that you would use to water plants. And it was for this group of us there of 100-odd persons, and we were supposed to drink that water from the pail and there would be dozens of us flocking to the pail to at least get our mouth wet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at the football pitch in your testimony you have estimated a number of persons you believe were present, can you please tell me how you arrive at this estimate; that is, what is the basis for your estimate of the number of persons that were present at the football pitch in Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: In my free estimate, picture a football pitch and its carrying capacity. At least 1.500 to 2.000 people can fit in a football pitch if seated. That was how I arrived at the number, and the pitch was full.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, in your Rule 92 per statement which is P1547, at page 5 in both languages, in the middle of the page, you discuss a speech by General Mladic. First I want to have you describe for us where this stage was located. Was it on the pitch itself or was it on the roadway?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: It was taken place in the pitch itself. When he came to us, when he approached us and we were seated on the ground, that was after the Serb soldiers escorted us through the gate and on to the pitch, and made us sit down, that was when he addressed us and it was all happening on the football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What material did the stage appear to be made of and how -- what were its dimensions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: I said that I didn't remember, and I stand by it. Was it a stage or was it some sort of elevation that was there from before, the only thing I know is that he was standing on high ground. He was overlooking us. And everybody was able to see him. Now, was it a stage? I don't know. At any rate, it was at one end and I did mark it on that sketch.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, how long did General Mladic stay there and address the persons assembled at the soccer -- at the football pitch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Well, he didn't stay very long. As soon as he appeared there, he addressed us, he said who he was, and then he began asking us where we were headed and all that, and then he went out in front of us and said a few words, not very long, not longer than ten minutes at most.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You describe that he arrived in an armoured personnel carrier and that the same was located approximately 100 metres from you. Did this armoured personnel carrier have wheels or a track?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: There was a correction made yesterday, I believe. I'm not sure whether it was a tracked vehicle or whether it had wheels. I only saw it when it was passing by me some ten metres away, and when he addressed us. So what type of vehicle it was, I'm not really sure and I can't confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall how many doors it had on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Well, try to put yourself in my shoes. Would you have time to think about how many doors that vehicle had or what type of vehicle it was? It was a matter of survival so I wasn't really paying any attention to what kind of vehicle it was so I can't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now I want to move to what you recall General Mladic's words were. In your Rule 92 ter statement that we have up on the screen you state as follows, and it's paragraph 20 if you want to follow along, and you say: "First, Mladic asked do you know me? Some said, Yes, and others were quiet. He said, I am the general, Ratko Mladic. Where were you going, what was your goal? Where is your state? Where is Alija Izetbegovic and Silajdzic? Where are your commanders Naser and Zulfo Tursunovic. You do not have your state here. You have to go look for your state. You sent your women to be protected by UNPROFOR while you're killing our soldiers. None can pass through because we have knitted a net with our soldiers, they are close together and have dogs. You do not have to worry. You will be exchanged and join your families in Tuzla. Now you'll be transported by trucks to Bratunac or Kravica where you will spend the night and get some food." And the question I want to ask you, sir, is: Do you really stand by every word that is printed here as truthfully and accurately reflecting what you remember Mladic to have said on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that, and this is true. All of this is true. And I will never forget this for as long as I live. Everything I've said there is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we received an information report from the Prosecutor's office dated 27 January 1998 - it's signed by the OTP investigators for January 1999 - reflecting what you had corrected that you did not know whether General Mladic mentioned Bratunac as is indicated in this paragraph. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: No. I didn't really understand what you are saying. I don't see that Bratunac is mentioned anywhere. Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in the part that we just read at paragraph 20 of your statement, Bratunac is mentioned in both the B/C/S and the English. And my question to you, sir, was that we have an information report from the Prosecution indicating that you corrected this part of the paragraph to remove the reference to Bratunac. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: I don't really remember. It's possible. But he said, You will be received by our soldiers. You will be accommodated. You will get food and water. I don't know about Bratunac specifically. I see it in the statement so it's possible that he did say it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And now here in paragraph 20, the part that I just read and that you just confirmed, you also have this phrase: "You sent your women to be protected by UNPROFOR while you're killing our soldiers." And I want to ask you, in relation to the speech given by General Mladic at Kasaba, you have given other statements in your own language to various BiH organs including the 19 July 1995 statement that we have looked at, also one to an investigative judge 27 July 1995, another dated 28 July 1995, and one dated 3 August 1995. Now, I've read all these, and in none of these statements do I find this language that I have just highlighted for you that appears in your ICTY statement which is taken just a few days after the last of these statements to the BiH authorities. Can you tell us or explain to us how it was that this language only appears in your ICTY statement of August 1995, the language as to: "You sent your women to be protected by UNPROFOR while you're killing our soldiers"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: I think that that language can be found in every one of my statements. You sent your women and children to UNPROFOR while you're killing our soldiers. And I believe this language is in each and every one of my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I could have 1D1031, it's page 3 in both languages, and in the B/C/S it is at the top of the page whereas in the English it is in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the gist of the last question is that this language does not appear in any of the other statements as put on paper. Is there any dispute about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd want to check each of them before coming back to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if you would follow along with me, the part I'd like to focus on reads as follows: "On that occasion, an improvised stage was set up near the road, and at one moment the Chetnik general, Ratko Mladic, who had come in a personnel carrier, addressed us from the stage. He said the following words: 'Do you know who I am?' Some then said they did and some kept silent. He then talked to us, saying he was Ratko Mladic. Then he asked us why we were fighting in vain and said we were recklessly following Alija, Silajdzic and the other leaders and losing our lives. He then asked, 'Where is your Naser? I took him by helicopter to Sarajevo. Where is your Zulfo? Here are his documents. How many thousand German marks did he take with him? Does he know that he cannot pass through my lines?' On that occasion he also told us that he would exchange all of us disregarding that each of us was, that nobody would be hurt and that we would be reunited with our families. After the speech he got into his personnel carrier and set off in the direction of Konjevic Polje." I apologise, I'm told that's page 3 of the B/C/S which I thought was what I had read and it should be at the top of the page. We have page 2 up on the screen. Sir, does that selection from your 1995 July 19 statement refresh your recollection as to whether the text "you sent your women to be protected by UNPROFOR while you're killing our soldiers" was indeed something that you added at the time that the ICTY statement was generated for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS RM253
utterances.text: No, no. I claim with full responsibility that I did not add that sentence. He said: "You sent your wife and children to UNPROFOR while you're killing our soldier. Not a single soldier will get through, and if you have any family members, call them, tell them to come out of the woods lest they be killed there." And I've said this on every occasion, there were several statements that I provided, and perhaps a word or two may have been omitted, or I don't know how it was translated, but I do state and claim with full responsibility that this is what he said and I will never recant that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, rather than going through all the statements I would invite the Office of the Prosecutor to stipulate that it's neither of those four prior statements, once I've had a chance to review the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We will come back to that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, we are about three minutes from adjourning for the day. I'd like to read a brief statement on behalf of the Chamber, and rather than to go first in closed session then in open session again I'd rather do it now when we are still in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we will adjourn later on in closed session. The Chamber turns now to the issue of the Defence's request for a reduction in the trial sitting schedule. On the 4th of June this year, the Chamber held an administrative hearing to put questions to Dr. Falke with regard to the health of the accused as it relates to the request to sit four days a week. During the hearing, and I refer to transcript page 12029, the Chamber asked Dr. Falke, and thereby the Registry, to provide the Chamber with written observations from the accused's physiotherapy treatments and, at page 12047, a list of the weight measurements taken for the accused. The Chamber expects to receive this information as soon as possible. Also during the administrative hearing the Chamber requested the parties to make any additional submissions in writing by 7th of June, 2013, which the Prosecution did, filing an addendum to its response. The Defence did not, if the Chamber is well-informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's my understanding, although I wasn't here for the hearing, I did speak with Mr. Lukic about that earlier, and I believe we will not be filing any additional written response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then that is clear why we did not receive it. The Chamber is currently considering all of the submissions on the matter and will issue its decision in due course. Until then, at least until then, the Chamber has decided to continue the existing sitting schedule of five days a week with the exception of the first week of July, when the Chamber will sit for four days with Monday, the 1st July, being a non-sitting day, although due to matters unrelated to the medical issue raised. And this concludes the Chamber's announcement with regard to the trial schedule. We will adjourn soon, once we are in closed session. We will adjourn and resume on Wednesday, the 12th of June, 2013, same Courtroom I at 9.30 in the morning. Meanwhile, we can turn into closed session but I hereby instruct you, Witness, that you should not speak or communicate in whatever way with whomever about your testimony, whether that is testimony already given or testimony still to be given. Waiting for being in closed session, Mr. Ivetic, could you give us an indication as to how much more time you will need.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 20 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 12th day of June 2013, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.16 p.m.,
